report:
**Conclusion**  
Your sister’s view is supported by strong scientific evidence: add-on (adjunctive) pharmaceutical-grade cannabidiol (CBD) significantly reduces convulsive seizure frequency in children and young adults with Dravet syndrome, a severe form of drug-resistant epilepsy.

**Key Evidence**  
* **Landmark Clinical Trial:** A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial published in *The New England Journal of Medicine* evaluated CBD added to existing antiepileptic medications. Patients receiving add-on cannabidiol saw their median monthly convulsive seizure frequency drop from 12.4 to 5.9, compared to a minimal drop from 14.9 to 14.1 in the placebo group.
* **FDA Approval:** Based on these randomized trials, the U.S. FDA approved Epidiolex (a plant-derived oral CBD solution) as an adjunctive treatment for Dravet syndrome.
* **Systematic Evidence:** Systematic reviews and dose-ranging trials confirm that add-on CBD (at doses such as 10 mg/kg/day and 20 mg/kg/day) provides clinically meaningful reductions in convulsive seizures compared to usual care alone.

While effective, CBD can interact with other antiepileptic medications and cause side effects (such as fatigue, decreased appetite, or elevated liver enzymes), so it requires medical supervision.

**Sources**
* *The New England Journal of Medicine* Trial: https://www.nejm.org/doi/10.1056/NEJMoa1611618?url_ver=Z39.88-2003&rfr_id=ori:rid:crossref.org&rfr_dat=cr_pub++0www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov
* FDA Drug Label: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/210365lbl.pdf
* Systematic Review in *CNS Drugs*: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40263-020-00708-6
* Clinical Review: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7439947/
